note: Engine divergences from book/src/session-lifecycle.md:256 (shipped anomalies 1/2/3/5) plus the C1/C2 deployed-compatible behaviors. A mixed-pair mismatch whose field+engine+call matches an entry is RECORDED, not failed; the entry states the healing condition. Anything else is a finding.

entries.title: Deployed Rust opens A.5 on its own send-PQ leaf lag and never opens the reciprocal
entries.healing: Healed by spec behavior: the deployed responder Commit' carries its current credential, so a conforming peer's reciprocal A.5 completes the catch-up and the loop stops.

entries.title: Deployed born-dedicated acceptor never catches up its leaf in the initiator's send-PQ group
entries.healing: Healed once the acceptor runs a conforming engine; the peer cannot heal it, since only the acceptor's own Upd' moves that leaf.

entries.title: Folding a caught-up/catch-up Upd: the deployed engine accepts or rejects where the conforming engine differs (proposing == sender)
entries.healing: Healed by the peer's host: a conforming engine marks such an offer as a catch-up, which the host approves without authorizing a new credential.

entries.title: Deployed A.3 bind joins signing with its current PQ key, not the KP' key its leaf presents
entries.healing: Needs an accommodation: the deployed-compatible profile's deferred reciprocal (C2). Once the leaf is orphaned, nothing heals it.

entries.title: Deployed-compatible responder returns the announced id; a conforming session with the deployed engine logs it
entries.healing: Compatibility behavior, not a defect: the announced id is read to trigger reconciliation; both profiles accept an Upd' whose authenticated data is empty or equals the new leaf's credential id. Scoped to deliverSideBand ONLY: the announced id is a side-band (A.5) behavior, so this entry must never excuse a hadOffer mismatch on the plain message path (that is the un-root-caused offer-surfacing divergence, and it must fail).

entries.title: The reciprocal A.5 waits until the peer's own A.5 has landed
entries.healing: Compatibility behavior: against a conforming peer it costs at most one extra round. A conforming engine taking the party over drops its mis-signed parked Upd' and re-proposes under the carried key.

entries.title: On an approved handoff frame Rust surfaces the stapled app payload while Swift's .joined carries none
entries.healing: Canonical rule: payloads accumulate separately from `joined`. Scoped to the `deliverApproved` call ONLY — the approved-handoff path this harness does not yet drive (born-dedicated/approved driving is deferred), so the entry is INERT today and cannot swallow signal. When that path lands, the plan's mandate is that this asymmetry surfaces as a finding first, not that it is suppressed; re-evaluate this entry then.

entries.title: The conforming Swift engine refuses a second rotation while one is un-canonicalized (.rotationInFlight); the deployed Rust engine permits it
entries.healing: Rotation-trigger family (anomaly 1). The deployed engine's lazy staging admits a candidate with no in-flight guard; a conforming host proposes a rotation only when none is outstanding, so against the deployed engine this surfaces as a permitted rotation it would otherwise defer.
